proposed.sourceName: South African National Halaal Authority (SANHA) — E472(e) Acetyltartaric Acid Glycerol Esters
proposed.paraphrase: SANHA classifies E472(e)/DATEM as Mushbooh (doubtful): it is esters of acetic acid, glycerol, tartaric acid and fatty acids, so the source of the glycerol and fatty acids (plant oil vs animal/pork fat) must be checked to determine halal status.

proposed.sourceName: American Halal Foundation (AHF) — 'Are Mono Diglycerides Halal?' (Azmi Anees)
proposed.paraphrase: AHF notes mono/diglycerides (the fatty-acid backbone of E472 esters) may derive from plant oils, halal-slaughtered beef, non-zabiha beef, or pork; the pork-derived possibility is never halal and the chemical change is not considered complete, so undisclosed-origin ester emulsifiers remain doubtful (avoid unless labeled vegetable or halal-certified) rather than presumptively permissible.

researcherNote: E472 seeded lenient grade 3 (contested). Kept doubtful, not accepted: pork-derived esters are never cleared even leniently (AHF); SANHA advises verifying the source. Two independent tier-1. APPROVED by owner 2026-07-01 (batch pre-approval).
